runs.text: A capstone proposal for evaluating retail agents
with controlled tools and verifiable evidence

This presentation explains the proposed capstone and a source-based walkthrough of tau2-bench. The retail example comes from the base task collection at commit 122e2432b82d740e8f313f46f0a071729c404f39. The walkthrough is a source-code reconstruction, not a recorded model run. Proposed components and experiments are labeled throughout.
Evaluate interchangeable retail agents against explicit business rules
Did the agent complete the task?
Check the actual order, refund and inventory state.
Did it act within its authority?
Check confirmation, policy limits and approval evidence.
Planned scope: returns, exchanges and coupon rules in a synthetic store.

The project targets observable outcomes and process compliance. A successful-looking reply is insufficient. The proposal includes a synthetic store, controlled tools, a policy guard, prompt optimization and single-step reinforcement learning. This is a personal capstone project, not an employer deployment. Source: local capstone SCOPE.md and Proposal v2 dated October 24, 2026.

The standard agent interface separates decision-making from tool execution.

The agent receives policy, tool definitions and conversation/tool messages. The user simulator receives the user scenario. The orchestrator routes messages and tool requests. Standard adapters should not execute a write internally and then submit the same write to the orchestrator. In-process callable tools are not a security sandbox.
Base retail task 0: exchange two items in one delivered order
A clicky, full-size keyboard with RGB lighting.
A thermostat compatible with Google Home instead of Apple HomeKit.
Customer knows name and ZIP code, but has forgotten the email address.

Yusuf Rossi, ZIP 19122, wants a keyboard and thermostat exchange. The task asks the simulated customer to address everything in one go. The order is delivered. The customer requests Google Home compatibility, while the product data labels the target variant Google Assistant. This distinction is preserved in later slides.

A normal tested agent discovers the solution through dialogue and tools.

The reference actions are not a mandatory script. They identify the user, read the order, read two products and request one combined exchange. Normal LLMAgent behavior does not use the reference solution as its prompt. Ground-truth/debug agents are a separate condition and must not be presented as an ordinary baseline. Task 0 has null natural-language assertions.
Each tool result becomes evidence for the next agent decision
The agent combines the message with policy, tools and conversation history.
Return a reply or a tool request
The model proposes an action. It has not changed the database yet.
The orchestrator calls the environment and sends the tool result back.

LLMAgent.generate_next_message appends the incoming message and calls generate with model, tools and message history. Orchestrator.step routes ordinary replies to the user and tool calls to the environment. _execute_tool_calls calls environment.get_response. The trajectory retains requests and results. This cycle repeats until the conversation stops or a limit/error ends the run.
The preferred RGB keyboard exists, but it is unavailable
The agent should explain both replacements and obtain confirmation.

Keyboard old item 1151293680 maps to new item 7706410293. Thermostat old item 4983901480 maps to new item 7747408585. The clicky RGB full-size keyboard has available=false. The accepted fallback is clicky, no backlight, full-size. Arithmetic: 269.16 - 272.33 + 249.01 - 262.47 = -16.63. The negative difference records the exchange price difference, not completed bank settlement.
One request includes both items and their corresponding replacements
The tool checks order status, item membership, replacement availability
and the payment method before changing state.

This slide shows an abbreviated tool-call payload. Actual identifiers are strings, including item IDs. The function requires delivered status, checks item multiplicities and matching list lengths, resolves each new variant within the old product, checks availability and validates payment. A gift-card payment must cover a positive price difference. The function does not receive a user-confirmation token.

The write changes order fields rather than completing fulfillment

A second exchange call fails the delivered-status check.

The tool mutates the in-memory Order model in the retail environment. It records sorted item lists, payment method and the price difference. It does not replace order.items, ship products or settle a bank refund in this function. Since status becomes exchange requested, splitting the two exchanges into separate calls would cause the later call to fail the delivered-status requirement.
The evaluator builds an actual state and a reference state independently
Create a fresh environment and replay recorded state-changing calls.
Create another fresh environment and execute the reference actions.
For task 0, empty NL assertions contribute 1. Normal completion leaves DB as the deciding score.

EnvironmentEvaluator applies initialization data and actions, reconstructs predicted state from the full trajectory, and constructs gold state from initial history plus reference actions. It compares both agent and user DB hashes. set_state skips non-mutating calls and rejected calls and checks replay output in strict mode. Task 0 basis is DB + NL_ASSERTION, but nl_assertions is null, yielding neutral 1. Premature termination produces 0 before component evaluation. This is task-specific, not a claim that all tau2 tasks use DB-only grading.
A correct final state can hide a process violation
Hypothetical comparison: identical final states, different confirmation behavior
Proposed addition: verify a trusted confirmation event before the write.

This comparison is a hypothetical source-based counterexample, not a measured model result. Assume both traces execute identical valid exchange calls and terminate normally. The tool has no confirmation credential argument, the DB comparison cannot prove confirmation, and this task has no nonempty NL assertion. Other tau2 tasks or added evaluators may check dialogue requirements. A proposed deterministic confirmation check must rely on trusted evidence bound to the action, rather than an agent-supplied confirmed=true claim.

Report agent violations separately from violations the guard prevents.

This slide describes a proposed architecture, not completed integration. Original retail lacks delivered-date and coupon models needed by the capstone. A custom commerce domain is a candidate. Existing FinePrint includes SQLite data, policy logic and an independent final-state verifier, but event-level approval and authorization checks need further work. External MCP calls require a controlled gateway and trustworthy state/log collection. Tool-call logging alone does not guarantee reproducible replay. Source: capstone SCOPE.md, tau2-learning-notes.zh.md, and FinePrint verify.py.

These are proposal targets, not completed evaluations. There are five conditions: handwritten baseline, GEPA, MIPROv2, GRPO and frontier reference. Preserve task and rule-combination splits, tool access, observation boundaries and budgets. Include do-nothing, always-ask and always-escalate controls and Guard on/off. pass^k estimates all k trials succeeding: C(c,k)/C(n,k), then averages per task. It does not establish production readiness. Report paired uncertainty and human review of simulated conversations. Source: capstone SCOPE.md.

Suggested sequence, not a claim of completed implementation. Start with a return-window rule and inside/outside/boundary cases, then adversarial traces. Inspect both attempted actions and actual state changes. After the environment and verifier are credible, connect LLM agents, compare conditions and investigate failures. Memory, seller A2A and retrieval are later extensions in the proposal. Source: capstone SCOPE.md and tau2-learning-notes.zh.md.
